title: The unskilled guide destroys; the skilled guide heals
english: An unskilled pilot is a shipwreck waiting to happen, and an ignorant leader is the destruction of his disciples. An inexperienced shepherd has twisted the ankles of his sheep, and a leader twists the paths of his disciples. An ignorant shepherd will not discern among sheep in the fog, nor will an inexperienced teacher say anything useful in a time of trial. A skilled leader is a general in war and a physician of the passions: he will either keep a man from being wounded or heal him quickly once he is wounded. A disobedient disciple is a warped piece of wood, and he will never be straightened no matter how often he is reproved. A discordant brother is a string on an out-of-tune lyre, and by his discord he is cut off from the common melody. A drone eats the labors of the bees, and a careless brother diminishes the virtuous practice of the community.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG De magistris et discipulis u01-open
orientation: Evagrius opens the treatise by addressing the monastic leader directly, comparing unskilled and skilled guides through a series of parallel images.
